note: Questions the app offers. The first two are the hero cards; the others come from the night scan's divergence ledger.

questions.label: Semaglutide (Ozempic, Rybelsus, Wegovy) and sudden vision loss (NAION)
questions.hook: Europe and the UK now warn that semaglutide can, very rarely, cause sudden vision loss. The U.S. label doesn't.

questions.reaction: sexual dysfunction that persists after stopping the drug
questions.label: Sertraline (Zoloft) and sexual dysfunction that persists after stopping
questions.hook: Europe has warned since 2019 that sexual problems can continue after stopping SSRIs. In October 2026 the UK said it will add the term PSSD to patient leaflets.

questions.label: Darolutamide (Nubeqa) and angioedema
questions.hook: In June 2026 PRAC recommended adding angioedema to darolutamide's EU product information (the company then has two months to apply for the change).

questions.reaction: DRESS (drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms)
questions.label: Gemcitabine and DRESS
questions.hook: In June 2026 PRAC recommended adding DRESS to the EU product information of gemcitabine medicines (the companies then have two months to apply for the change).

questions.reaction: neurodevelopmental disorders in children of fathers treated with valproate
questions.label: Valproate taken by fathers and neurodevelopmental disorders in their children
questions.hook: Since 2024 Europe and the UK have told men taking valproate to use contraception, because of a possible risk to their children. In June 2026 PRAC re-reviewed newer, mixed studies: it kept those measures and asked for the product information to say the evidence is inconsistent.
questions.note: first EU action January 2024 (CMDh endorsed PRAC's precautionary measures), UK Drug Safety Update 5 September 2024; the June 2026 PRAC entry in the night-scan ledger is a re-review
